newsitem.title: FINLAND: SILJA, VIKING SEE FAIRWAY FEE HIKE INCREASING COSTS.
newsitem.headline: SILJA, VIKING SEE FAIRWAY FEE HIKE INCREASING COSTS.

text.p: Finnish ferry operators Silja Oy Ab and Viking Line Ab said on Thursday an announced 20 percent hike in Finnish fairway fees will increase their annual domestic fairway costs by millions of markka.
"Silja's fairway costs in Finland (in 1996) were 26 million markka, so there will be an additional cost of 5.2 million markka," Silja director Christian Gronvall told Reuters.
He was asked to comment on the government's decision on Monday to increase fairway fees by 20 percent on January 1.
Gronvall said the increase in fairway costs could weigh on the group's 1997 earnings unless it could be transferred to ticket prices.
In January-September 1996, Silja had a 32 million markka loss after financial items, up from a 250 million markka loss in the first nine months of 1995.

Nils-Erik Eklund, CEO of Silja's rival Viking Line AB, said the higher fairway fees are expected to increase the passenger ferry operator's annual domestic fairway costs by about three million markka from less than 18 million.
Finnish fairway fees are higher than those in Sweden, Eklund said, but did not give details.
"Finnish fairway fees are probably the highest in the world," he said.
Nobody at Finnish cargo ship company Finnlines Oy was immediately available for comment.
The Ministry of Transport and Communications said earlier state revenues from fairway fees are expected to rise to about 402 million markka in 1997 from about 333 million markka in 1996.
